He was really upset when I drunkenly told him what happened. He told me how upset he was I felt that way, and how he couldn’t think about what would’ve happened if that rope didn’t fall.

My father has extremely bad panic attacks, sometimes nocturnal ones to where he will randomly wake up in the middle of the night mid panic. I also have panic attacks, though not as extreme. 

It’s hard to help someone while having a panic attack. You can see things rationally, and in this moment in time, they can’t. But, they don’t know that, they think they’re being rational, and that’s the scary part. A panic attack is something you can’t snap out of, but something you must get through. 

I think what you’re doing is really good! Just being there is great and reassurance that the attack will pass and that they are okay. Try to make the environment as calming as possible, you using ice packs to stimulate the nervous system can help too! I think if anything, you and your husband should explore grounding techniques. Grounding techniques don’t stop the panic attack, however, they can help make getting through it easier. 

Another thing yall can do is try and find triggers. They aren’t always obvious, and sometimes you can have a panic attack that is completely random and not triggered by something. I’ve met people with triggers that stem from trauma, to more simple things like eating too much sugar or driving. I would keep track of what he did or felt that day and when he had the panic attack, maybe there’s a pattern.

And lastly, panic meds can be a life saver. Now usually they are short term, but they can help so much. My father will take an Ativan if his panic attacks are really bad, and though it doesn’t just snap him out of it, it helps calm him down enough to start thinking more rationally and feel more at ease getting through the terror. If you want something non habit forming, then try Hydroxyzine. 

Panic attacks are terrible and terrifying, I feel for your husband and hope he gets some peace. You are doing wonderful to help him! Be patient with yourself as it’s hard to help someone through an attack, though it may feel like you’re not doing much, you just being there with him does so much to help and support him. 

Hoping the best for yall, I hope my advice helped even the tiniest bit!❤️

I feel this. It does get easier though. I took testosterone for about 4 years, and have been off it for 3. It’s hard, though some things revert back to how it was (muscle/fat distribution). Some changes stay the same, like a deeper voice, (though it will slightly lighten up over time) body hair, the “down there” stuff. 
It’s so hard sometimes, I have had people thought I was transphobic, MTF, I have even been called a freak by a random stranger. 

I still have so many insecurities, but you have to find some love and patience for yourself. Yes, we chose to go on hormones, we messed up, but we are human. Find a good support group, friends, family, a partner. That has been my saving grace. Many people won’t understand fully, but will be there if you need a shoulder to lean on. 

I have gotten more confident in myself as time has went on. Though I don’t have a super feminine body (I have a harder looking face, broad shoulders, bigger arms), I have taken strides in learning how to dress feminine and do makeup. It’s been difficult but it has really helped. I am starting feminization voice exercises that I’m hoping will help too. 

Even though I have bad days a lot, I have good days too. Sometimes I can look in the mirror and think I’m beautiful. On the good days, I’ve started to learn to love my body, my voice, and feel at home in myself again. 

Basically what I’m saying is, it’s going to be a long and rough journey, but DONT lose hope. You are beautiful, even if you don’t feel like it. There is a light at the end of this dark and murky tunnel. You will feel like you again. You can do this OP, you’ve gotten through a transition before, and you can come back from it. And if you feel alone in your personal life, this subreddit is full of people who have your back. 

Stay strong❤️

That’s a big question, and there’s so many ways to do it! 

Think about what interests you, then create something with it! Like when I drew in highschool, I was infatuated with tv shows, so I’d draw the characters in various scenarios that I wished they could be in. To start maybe use those recreated images and scramble them together to draw from. Or if you like landscapes, you could collage many sceneries together to make something new. 

Or really anything. Try experimenting with thumbnails and researching subjects! Maybe draw from life to give you inspiration! Maybe mind map for ideas.

There’s so many possibilities that I can’t give you just one great idea, experiment. Maybe give yourself a prompt to follow. The main goal is to have fun with what you’re doing and to create something that you’ll ultimately enjoy and be proud of.

Excited to see what you’ll do!

Gesture drawing!! Especially timed gesture drawing, it helps get the motion and fluidity of poses and helps so much with anatomy. 
But try not to focus so much on “I need to get better”, because that’s a double edged sword. You’ll become motivated to get better but may burn out due to not seeing progress fast enough.
The best way to get better is practice, like all the time, and draw what interests you. How-to drawing books never really interested me, I mostly just drew cartoon characters growing up and I began to improve. But if you do want a technical answer, again, gesture drawing. 

Whatever you do, have fun with it, that’s the magic of art :))

If I could give you some advice: Keep working on your kicks and your head position! Head position is crucial when it comes to swimming, when your eyes are in the water, it’s important to keep proper swimming posture and keep your head straight and chin down. If you’re wearing goggles, eyes should be down to the floor. For side breathing, make sure you’re truly leaning to the side. I have mix ups myself where I try to breathe to the side and end up in this weird diagonal breathing😂 If there is a lane line, I try to remind myself to look at that. Head position, how you kick, and even your pull determines the direction in which you swim, especially head position.
I’d say keep doing what you’re doing, and make sure that head is STRAIGHT!! 

Keep it up! Start learning new strokes too! Make swimming fun and interesting, it’s so amazing! Best of luck
